parsed.faithful: On the death of Archelaus, the kingdom of Cappadocia was reduced to a Roman province, and governed by those of the equestrian order. It continued subject to the Romans till the invasion of the eastern empire by the Turks, to whom it is now subject, but has no distinguishing modern name. In what was anciently called Cappadocia, however, the Turks have four Beglerbegliks, called Siwas, Trekiand, Marash, and Cogni.
